After splitting spawn and wait, managed owner-transfer discovery did not recurse through an EnumMatch subject or resolve the instance flow target, so the successful wait arm could still drop the consumed outer Result<Child, Text> a second time. Selfhost movesFrom likewise scanned declared kind-6 calls but not value-producing kind-9 process intrinsics, so enum-arm cleanup directly dropped a Child already consumed by wait.

defects.owner: managed and self-host browser wall-clock runtime capability
defects.rootCause: The wasm32 browser runtime implements both sollang_now_millis and sollang_utc_now_millis by calling the single sollang_browser_now_millis host import. The browser host maps that import to performance.now(), which is a monotonic process/page-relative reading rather than Unix epoch time. std.time.WallClock.now therefore returns a value that is neither UTC nor serializable as the documented UtcInstant on browser targets, while Windows and Linux use distinct wall-clock primitives.
defects.focusedFixture: A browser time-domain fixture must read MonotonicClock and WallClock from distinct host imports, prove that the wall value is a Unix epoch millisecond instant while monotonic elapsed time remains nondecreasing, and reject a host that omits either declared capability. Managed and self-host wasm LLVM must expose identical imports and exact execution through the real compiler-client host.
defects.closureGate: Introduce a distinct sollang_browser_utc_now_millis host capability backed by Date.now(), retain performance.now() only for monotonic time, update managed and self-host wasm runtimes plus both browser host import tables, and add direct-call closure, wasm assembly, exact host execution, warning/note zero, Stage2/Stage3 browser parity, and public playground verification. Do not alias, synthesize, or silently fall back between the two domains.
closedEvidence: The current managed WasmBrowserLlvmRuntimePlatform emits sollang_utc_now_millis by calling sollang_browser_now_millis, and both compiler-client import tables implement that host function with Math.trunc(performance.now()).

The current Windows runtime uses GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime for UTC and GetTickCount64 for monotonic time; Linux likewise separates CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC. This proves the browser behavior is a target-specific parity defect rather than the intended public contract.
Managed and self-host browser emitters now declare distinct monotonic and UTC imports, and all four host import tables map them to performance.now() and Date.now() respectively.
